title: Payment API returns HTTP 500
symptoms: Payment requests fail with Internal Server Error
Checkout payment service gives a 500 error
diagnostic_checks: Capture the failed request ID and timestamp without payment details.
Review application logs for the correlated exception.
Check payment dependencies and connection pool health.
Compare the start of failures with recent deployments.
resolution: If logs identify a failing dependency, restore that dependency using its approved runbook. If a deployment regression is confirmed, request an approved rollback. HTTP 500 alone does not establish a root cause.

title: Database connection failure
symptoms: Cannot connect to the database
SQL connection refused or connection timeout
diagnostic_checks: Record the exact database connection error and affected service.
Check database availability and the configured host and port.
Verify network reachability from the application environment.
Check credential validity through the approved secret manager without exposing secrets.
resolution: Correct a verified host or port mismatch through the approved configuration process. Route network, database availability, or credential failures to the responsible owner after confirming the error.

title: Application pages load slowly
symptoms: The application takes too long to load
Pages are slow and response latency is high
diagnostic_checks: Measure response times and identify affected endpoints.
Compare application CPU, memory, and dependency latency with the normal baseline.
Inspect slow request traces and slow database queries.
Check whether traffic or a recent release changed.
resolution: Address a measured bottleneck through its owning team. Request a reviewed query or capacity change only when the metrics support it.

title: Login fails with invalid credentials
symptoms: Users cannot log in
Authentication failed or invalid username password
diagnostic_checks: Record the exact login error without recording the password.
Determine whether one account or all accounts are affected.
Check account lock status and identity provider health.
Confirm the user is using the intended environment.
resolution: If an account lock or expired credential is confirmed, use the approved account recovery process. For widespread failures, escalate identity provider evidence.

title: Disk space running low
symptoms: No space left on device
Disk is full and writes fail
diagnostic_checks: Identify the affected filesystem and available capacity.
Inspect directory usage and log growth using approved read-only tools.
Check retention settings and whether files are still in use.
resolution: Request approved log rotation, retention cleanup, or storage expansion after identifying the source of growth. Do not delete unknown or active application files.

title: Service unavailable HTTP 503
symptoms: Service is down with 503 Service Unavailable
Backend has no healthy instances
diagnostic_checks: Confirm the affected service and exact HTTP status.
Inspect health checks and backend instance availability.
Check load balancer routing and recent deployments.
resolution: If health-check or routing configuration is confirmed incorrect, request its correction. If no instances are healthy, escalate logs and health-check results to the service owner.

title: Network connectivity timeout
symptoms: Host unreachable
Network connection timed out between servers
diagnostic_checks: Record source, destination, port, and failure time.
Compare reachability from an approved test location.
Review route and firewall changes with the network owner.
resolution: Have the network team correct a verified route or firewall problem through change control. A timeout alone cannot identify the faulty component.

title: Scheduled batch job failed
symptoms: Nightly scheduled job did not complete
Cron batch task failed
diagnostic_checks: Inspect scheduler status and the last execution log.
Check input availability, exit code, and runtime permissions.
Determine whether a previous run partially processed records.
resolution: After fixing a confirmed prerequisite failure, rerun only with the job owner's approval and verified duplicate-processing safeguards.

title: Invalid application configuration
symptoms: Application startup fails after configuration change
Missing environment variable or invalid config
diagnostic_checks: Capture the startup validation error without secret values.
Compare required variable names with the deployment specification.
Review recent configuration changes and the intended environment.
resolution: Correct the verified missing or invalid setting using the approved deployment workflow. Request a restart only if the service's runbook requires it.

title: High CPU utilization
symptoms: CPU usage stays at 100 percent
Processor saturation on application host
diagnostic_checks: Confirm sustained CPU usage rather than a brief spike.
Identify the process using CPU and correlate it with request volume.
Inspect approved profiling data and recent releases.
resolution: Escalate evidence of a hot process or workload spike. Use reviewed scaling or code changes after the bottleneck is established; do not kill processes solely from CPU usage.

title: Memory exhaustion or OOM termination
symptoms: Container killed due to out of memory
OOMKilled process or memory usage increasing
diagnostic_checks: Inspect termination reason and memory usage history.
Compare configured limits with baseline consumption.
Check workload growth and recent deployments.
resolution: If a limit mismatch is confirmed, request an approved capacity adjustment. If memory grows continuously, route profiling evidence to the application owner for leak investigation.

title: TLS certificate expired
symptoms: HTTPS certificate has expired
SSL certificate validation fails
diagnostic_checks: Inspect certificate validity dates and hostname from an approved client.
Check the certificate chain and the client's system time.
Confirm which endpoint terminates TLS.
resolution: If expiry is confirmed, have the certificate owner renew and deploy the correct certificate and chain. Do not disable TLS validation.

title: API rate limit HTTP 429
symptoms: Too many requests response
API returns HTTP 429
diagnostic_checks: Capture response status and any Retry-After header.
Compare request volume with the documented client quota.
Check whether retries are amplifying traffic.
resolution: For confirmed quota exhaustion, respect Retry-After and request an approved bounded retry policy. Discuss quota changes with the API owner if normal demand exceeds the allowance.

title: DNS name resolution failure
symptoms: Could not resolve hostname
DNS NXDOMAIN or name resolution failed
diagnostic_checks: Record the exact hostname and resolver error.
Check the configured resolver and the expected DNS record.
Compare resolution from the affected environment and an approved reference environment.
resolution: Request correction of a verified DNS record or resolver configuration through the DNS owner. Do not replace names with hard-coded addresses as a general fix.

title: Access denied HTTP 403
symptoms: Authenticated user receives forbidden response
API returns HTTP 403 access denied
diagnostic_checks: Confirm the exact resource, authenticated identity, and HTTP status.
Compare assigned roles with the resource's documented access policy.
Check recent role or policy changes.
resolution: Request a least-privilege access correction only when the resource owner confirms authorization is appropriate. Do not bypass the access policy.
